intro: Hi! At A2 you read emails, messages and short news, and you scanned them for one answer. Now you read short articles and opinion pieces about life in Jakarta, work, food and transport. You'll learn three skills: finding the main idea, telling facts from the writer's opinions, and skimming a text fast to get the gist.
teachingNotes: Build on a2-reading-everyday: read the question first, scan for the answer, then read that sentence and the ones around it; compare the WHOLE option with the text (the same-words trap). B1 texts are short articles, blog posts, reviews and opinion pieces of 80–120 words on Indonesian adult topics: city life in Jakarta, remote work, local businesses, healthy food trends, MRT/KRL. Every answer comes from the text alone, never from general knowledge.

Main idea vs details: the main idea is the one message the whole paragraph or article supports. It is often the first sentence (topic sentence), sometimes the last as a conclusion (So…, That's why…, In the end…); in an article, the title and first paragraph usually give it. Details are examples (for example, like), numbers, names, dates, reasons (because) and quotes. Test: could it be a short title for the whole text, and does every other sentence support it? Learners know kalimat utama / kalimat penjelas and paragraf deduktif / induktif from Bahasa Indonesia at school: use that link. Common errors: picking an interesting detail (a number, a quote) as the main idea; picking an idea that is too broad ('Jakarta is a big city'); picking an option that uses the text's words but changes the meaning.

Fact vs opinion: a fact can be checked (a date, a number, a place, an event, a price, a survey result); an opinion is what someone thinks or feels, and other people can disagree. Opinion signals: I think, I believe, in my opinion, in my view, should / shouldn't, the best / the worst, judging adjectives (terrible, amazing, boring, delicious, comfortable), too + adjective (too expensive), probably / maybe. Common errors: thinking any sentence with a number is a fact (Rp50,000 is too much for bakso = opinion); treating a guess about the future (will probably…) as a fact; treating a quote ('…,' says Pak Hasan) as a fact when it is that person's opinion; thinking a confident or popular opinion is a fact. Indonesian: menurut saya = in my opinion / I think, sebaiknya = should, paling enak = the best / the tastiest. Keep it simple: 'Can I check it?' A fact can also be wrong; it is still checkable.

Skimming: reading fast for the gist (inti, gambaran umum) with a time limit, about 1 minute for 100–120 words: read the title, the first sentence of each paragraph and the last sentence, let the eyes run over names and numbers without stopping. Skim (what is it about?) is not scan (A2: find one piece of information, like a time or a price). Common error: reading word by word, translating every sentence in the head and stopping at every new word to use a dictionary. After skimming, read carefully only the parts the task needs.

Limits: texts use A0–A2 grammar only (present simple and continuous, past simple and continuous, present perfect with just/already/yet/ever, will, going to, should / have to / must, comparatives and superlatives, zero and first conditional). No passive, past perfect, reported speech, relative clauses, used to or second conditional in the texts; if a learner meets one elsewhere, treat it as a phrase to remember. Don't go into writer's purpose, tone, irony or essay structure (later levels). Typed main-idea answers: accept any short phrase with the same meaning; a typed answer in Indonesian shows understanding but asks for English.

keyPoints.title: Main idea and supporting details
keyPoints.explanation: The main idea is the one big message of a paragraph or article; the other sentences support it. It's often the first sentence, sometimes the last (So…, That's why…). Details are examples, numbers, names, dates, reasons and what people say. Test: could it be a short title for the whole text?

examples.en: Working from home saves time for many people in Jakarta.
examples.id: Bekerja dari rumah menghemat waktu bagi banyak orang di Jakarta. (ide pokok)

examples.en: Before 2020, Sari spent three hours a day in traffic.
examples.id: Sebelum 2020, Sari menghabiskan tiga jam sehari di kemacetan. (detail: contoh)

id.title: Ide pokok dan detail pendukung
id.explanation: Ide pokok (main idea) adalah satu pesan besar dari sebuah paragraf atau artikel; kalimat-kalimat lain mendukungnya. Biasanya ada di kalimat pertama, kadang di kalimat terakhir (So…, That's why…). Detail adalah contoh, angka, nama, tanggal, alasan, dan kata-kata seseorang. Tesnya: bisakah kalimat itu jadi judul pendek untuk seluruh teks?

keyPoints.title: Fact or opinion?
keyPoints.explanation: You can check a fact: a date, a number, a place, an event. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels, and other people can disagree. Opinion words: I think, in my opinion, should, the best, terrible, too expensive, probably. A number doesn't make a sentence a fact.

examples.id: MRT Jakarta mulai beroperasi tahun 2019. (fakta: bisa dicek)

examples.en: In my opinion, the MRT is the best way to get to work.
examples.id: Menurut saya, MRT adalah cara terbaik untuk berangkat kerja. (opini)

examples.en: Rp50,000 is too much for a bowl of bakso.
examples.id: Rp50.000 terlalu mahal untuk semangkuk bakso. (opini, walaupun ada angkanya)

id.title: Fakta atau opini?
id.explanation: Fakta bisa dicek: tanggal, angka, tempat, kejadian. Opini adalah apa yang dipikirkan atau dirasakan seseorang, dan orang lain bisa tidak setuju. Kata-kata opini: I think, in my opinion, should, the best, terrible, too expensive, probably. Ada angka di kalimat tidak otomatis membuatnya fakta.

keyPoints.title: Skimming for the gist
keyPoints.explanation: Skimming = reading fast for the gist (the general idea). Read the title, the first sentence of each paragraph and the last sentence; don't stop at new words or translate. Give yourself about 1 minute for 120 words. Scanning (A2) is different: you look for one piece of information.

examples.en: BIKE LANES ON JALAN SUDIRMAN: WHO USES THEM?
examples.id: Jalur sepeda di Jalan Sudirman: siapa yang memakainya? (judul = petunjuk inti)

examples.en: What is this text about, in a few words?
examples.id: Teks ini tentang apa, dalam beberapa kata? (pertanyaan setelah skimming)

id.title: Skimming untuk menangkap inti
id.explanation: Skimming = membaca cepat untuk menangkap inti (gist, gambaran umum). Baca judulnya, kalimat pertama setiap paragraf dan kalimat terakhir; jangan berhenti di kata baru dan jangan menerjemahkan. Beri dirimu waktu sekitar 1 menit untuk 120 kata. Scanning (A2) itu berbeda: kamu mencari satu informasi saja.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read: 'Jakarta's parks are getting busier. Tebet Eco Park opened in 2022, and on weekends families walk, run and have picnics there. Taman Literasi in Blok M is full of students with books and laptops. Even small parks near housing areas now have yoga classes on Sunday mornings.' Which sentence gives the main idea: the first or the last?
guidedPractice.hint: Which sentence could be a title for the whole text? The others are examples of parks.

guidedPractice.prompt: Is this a fact or an opinion? 'Ojek online apps are probably the most useful apps on any phone in Jakarta.'
guidedPractice.hint: Look for opinion words: probably, the most useful. Can you check this?

guidedPractice.prompt: Is this a fact or an opinion? 'Bogor and Depok are both on the KRL Bogor line.'
guidedPractice.hint: Can you check it on a KRL map? Are there any opinion words?

guidedPractice.prompt: You want the gist of a news article in one minute. What is the first thing you read?
guidedPractice.hint: It's at the top, often in big or capital letters.

independentPractice.prompt: Read: 'More young people in Jakarta are choosing healthy food. Salad shops are opening in malls, and many coffee shops now sell oat milk. On Instagram, photos of healthy lunch boxes get thousands of likes. Even some warung near offices sell brown rice for an extra Rp3,000.' What is the main idea? Write it in a few words.
expected: young people are choosing healthy food
more young people are choosing healthy food
more young people choose healthy food
young people in jakarta are choosing healthy food
healthy food is popular with young people
young people are eating healthy food
independentPractice.hint: Read the first sentence. Salad shops, oat milk, Instagram and brown rice are all examples.

independentPractice.prompt: Read: 'Warung Bu Sri opens at 6 am and closes at 2 pm. Her nasi uduk costs Rp15,000. It is the tastiest nasi uduk in Bekasi.' Which word in the last sentence shows an opinion? Write it.
independentPractice.hint: You can check times and prices. Which word is a judgement (paling…)?

independentPractice.prompt: You need the general idea of an article, fast. Do you skim or scan? Write one word.
independentPractice.hint: Scan = find one piece of information. Which one is for the general idea?

assessment.prompt: Read the article: 'FROM GARAGE TO BRAND · Five years ago, Bu Ratna made batik bags in her garage in Pekalongan. Today she has a small shop and twelve workers, and she sells shirts and scarves too. About 70% of her sales are online, mostly through Instagram and online marketplaces. Last year she started sending orders to Malaysia and Singapore. "I started with one sewing machine," she says. Her story shows that a small home business can grow into a real brand with the help of the internet.' What is the main idea of the article? Write it in a few words.
acceptableAnswers: a small home business can grow into a real brand with the help of the internet
a small home business can grow with the internet
a small home business can grow into a brand with the internet
a small business can grow with the internet
small businesses can grow with the internet
a small business can grow online
a home business can grow with the internet
a home business can grow online
a small business can become a real brand with the internet
a small home business can become a brand with the internet
the internet helps small businesses grow
the internet can help a small business grow
the internet helped her business grow
the internet helped bu ratnas business grow
her business grew with the internet
her business grew with the help of the internet
bu ratnas business grew with the internet
her small business became a brand with the internet
assessment.rubric: Correct: a small home business can grow (into a real brand) with the internet / online, in any words; 'Bu Ratna's business grew with the internet' is also correct. Growth without the internet ('her business grew', 'from garage to brand') = 70. Only a detail (twelve workers, 70% online, Instagram, Malaysia and Singapore, one sewing machine) = 0. Too broad ('batik is popular', 'the internet is useful') = 0. The right idea written in Indonesian = 70.

assessment.prompt: Read the article: 'THE KRL IS GETTING BUSIER · Every year, more and more people are taking the KRL to work. Ani takes the 6:15 train from Depok to Manggarai every weekday. "Two years ago I always had a seat. Now I stand for the whole trip," she says. At her station, the number of morning passengers has gone up from about 8,000 to 11,000 a day. Many passengers want more trains in the morning, but some say the stations need more space first.' The first sentence gives the main idea. Find a supporting detail: how many morning passengers does Ani's station have now?
assessment.rubric: Correct: about 11,000 (a day). '8,000' = 0 (that was the number before). '6:15' = 0 (that's Ani's train). 'from 8,000 to 11,000' = 80 (right number, but the question asks for now).

assessment.prompt: Read this sentence from a food blog: 'At Rp45,000, a smoothie bowl is far too expensive for a normal breakfast.' Is it a fact or an opinion? Write fact or opinion.
assessment.rubric: Correct: opinion. 'far too expensive' is the writer's judgement, and other people may think the price is fine. 'fact' = 0: the price is a number you can check, but the sentence judges it. 'opini' (right idea, in Indonesian) = 70.

assessment.prompt: Read a comment about the MRT Jakarta: '(1) The MRT opened in March 2019, from Lebak Bulus to Bundaran HI. (2) At first it had 13 stations. (3) In my view, it is the most comfortable way to travel in Jakarta. (4) In 2019 a ticket cost between Rp3,000 and Rp14,000.' Which sentence is the writer's opinion? Write its number.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 3 ('In my view' and 'the most comfortable' show a judgement). 1, 2 or 4 = 0: the date and route, the number of stations and the ticket prices can all be checked.

assessment.prompt: Skim this article in 30 seconds: read the title and the first sentence of each paragraph. 'THE CAFÉ IS THE NEW OFFICE · Every morning, Kopi Teman in Kemang is full of people with laptops. Freelancers, students and remote workers come at 9 and stay until the afternoon. / For many remote workers, a café is cheaper than a co-working space. A coffee costs about Rp30,000, and the Wi-Fi is free. / But some café owners are not happy about it. "One customer buys one coffee and stays for eight hours," says Bayu, the owner. Now he has a new rule: one drink every two hours.' What is the article mainly about? Write it in a few words.
acceptableAnswers: the cafe is the new office
assessment.rubric: Correct: people (remote workers, freelancers, students) working in cafés / cafés used as offices, in any words; adding 'and some owners are not happy' is fine. Only the owner's new rule = 50 (one part, not the gist). Only 'coffee', 'Wi-Fi' or 'Kemang' = 0. The right idea in Indonesian = 70.

assessment.prompt: Skim this opinion piece in 30 seconds: 'WHY I MISS THE OFFICE · For two years I worked from home, and at first I loved it: no traffic, no uniform, lunch in my own kitchen. But slowly, things changed. I talked to my colleagues only on video calls, and I often worked late at night. Last month my company asked us to choose: home or office. I chose the office, four days a week. The trip is long, but I feel like part of a team again. In my opinion, home is for living, not for working.' Where does the writer prefer to work now? Write home or office.
acceptableAnswers: the office four days a week
in the office four days a week
assessment.rubric: Correct: the office (the title, 'I chose the office' and the last sentence all say it). 'home' = 0: the writer loved it only at first.

blocks.text:
An **article** is a short text about one topic: a news story, a blog post, a review or an opinion piece. Every good paragraph has **one main idea** (the big message) and **supporting details** (the sentences to explain it or show it's true).
- The main idea is often the **first sentence**. Sometimes it comes **last**, as a conclusion: *So…*, *That's why…*, *In the end…*
- Details are **examples** (*for example*, *like*), **numbers**, **names**, **dates**, **reasons** (*because*) and **what people say** (*"…," says Budi*).
- In a whole article, the **title** and the **first paragraph** usually give the main idea of the text.

You know this from school: in Bahasa Indonesia it's *kalimat utama* and *kalimat penjelas*. A paragraph with the main idea first is *deduktif*; with the main idea last, *induktif*. English paragraphs work the same way.

id.text:
**Artikel** adalah teks pendek tentang satu topik: berita, tulisan blog, ulasan (review), atau tulisan opini. Setiap paragraf yang baik punya **satu ide pokok** (main idea: pesan besarnya) dan **detail pendukung** (supporting details: kalimat-kalimat yang menjelaskan atau membuktikannya).
- Ide pokok biasanya ada di **kalimat pertama**. Kadang di **akhir**, sebagai kesimpulan: *So…* (jadi), *That's why…* (itulah sebabnya), *In the end…* (akhirnya).
- Detail adalah **contoh** (*for example* = misalnya, *like* = seperti), **angka**, **nama**, **tanggal**, **alasan** (*because* = karena) dan **kata-kata seseorang** (*"…," says Budi* = kata Budi).
- Di artikel yang utuh, **judul** dan **paragraf pertama** biasanya memberi ide pokok seluruh teks.

Kamu sudah tahu ini dari sekolah: di pelajaran Bahasa Indonesia namanya *kalimat utama* dan *kalimat penjelas*. Paragraf dengan ide pokok di awal disebut *deduktif*; dengan ide pokok di akhir, *induktif*. Paragraf bahasa Inggris juga begitu.

rows.en: So, small changes can make a big difference.
rows.id: Jadi, perubahan kecil bisa membuat perbedaan besar.
rows.note: So… / That's why… often gives the main idea at the end

id.note: So… / That's why… sering memberi ide pokok di akhir

blocks.text:
**Three wrong answers to avoid** when you choose a main idea:
- **Too small:** one interesting detail (a number, a name, a quote). It's true, but it isn't the whole text.
- **Too big:** an idea wider than the text (*Jakarta is a big city*).
- **Same words, different meaning:** an option with the text's words, but with a new meaning: the text doesn't say it. Check the whole sentence, as you did at A2.

id.text:
**Tiga jawaban salah yang harus dihindari** saat memilih ide pokok:
- **Terlalu kecil:** satu detail yang menarik (angka, nama, kutipan). Benar, tapi bukan isi seluruh teks.
- **Terlalu besar:** ide yang lebih luas dari teksnya (*Jakarta is a big city* = Jakarta kota besar).
- **Kata sama, arti beda:** pilihan yang memakai kata-kata dari teks dalam kalimat baru yang tidak dikatakan teks. Cek seluruh kalimatnya, seperti di A2.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'Pak Joko starts work at 5 am. He often finishes after 10 pm, and he drives about 150 km a day. Life as an ojek online driver is long and tiring.' Which sentence is the main idea?
options: Pak Joko starts work at 5 am.
He drives about 150 km a day.
Life as an ojek online driver is long and tiring.
blocks.explain: The last sentence sums up the paragraph. Starting at 5 am and driving 150 km are details: they show why his life is long and tiring.

id.prompt: Baca: 'Pak Joko starts work at 5 am. He often finishes after 10 pm, and he drives about 150 km a day. Life as an ojek online driver is long and tiring.' Kalimat mana yang merupakan ide pokok?
id.explain: Kalimat terakhir merangkum paragrafnya (paragraf induktif). Mulai kerja jam 5 pagi dan menyetir 150 km adalah detail: keduanya menunjukkan kenapa hidupnya panjang dan melelahkan.

blocks.text:
You can check a **fact**: in a calendar, on a map, with a number, in a report. *The MRT Jakarta opened in 2019.* / *Tebet Eco Park is in South Jakarta.*
An **opinion** is what someone thinks or feels. You can't prove it, and other people can disagree. *The MRT is the nicest way to travel.* / *Tebet Eco Park is too crowded on Sundays.*

Articles mix facts and opinions. A good reader asks: **Can I check this?** If yes, it's a fact. If it's somebody's judgement, it's an opinion, even when the writer sounds very sure.

id.text:
**Fakta** adalah sesuatu yang bisa dicek: di kalender, di peta, dengan angka, di laporan. *The MRT Jakarta opened in 2019.* (MRT Jakarta mulai beroperasi tahun 2019.) / *Tebet Eco Park is in South Jakarta.* (Tebet Eco Park ada di Jakarta Selatan.)
**Opini** adalah apa yang dipikirkan atau dirasakan seseorang. Tidak bisa dibuktikan, dan orang lain bisa tidak setuju. *The MRT is the nicest way to travel.* (MRT adalah cara bepergian yang paling enak.) / *Tebet Eco Park is too crowded on Sundays.* (Tebet Eco Park terlalu ramai di hari Minggu.)

Artikel mencampur fakta dan opini. Pembaca yang baik bertanya: **Bisakah aku mengecek ini?** Kalau bisa, itu fakta. Kalau itu penilaian seseorang, itu opini, walaupun penulisnya terdengar sangat yakin.

rows.en: I think / I believe / I feel
rows.id: saya pikir / saya yakin / saya rasa

rows.en: In my opinion / In my view
the best / the worst / the most comfortable
rows.id: paling bagus / paling buruk / paling nyaman
luar biasa, buruk sekali, membosankan, enak

rows.en: opened in 2019 / costs Rp15,000 / has 13 stations

blocks.text:
**Traps:**
- **A number doesn't make a fact.** *Rp50,000 is too much for a bowl of bakso* has a number, but **too much** is a judgement: opinion.
- **A guess about the future is an opinion.** *Prices will probably go down next year*: nobody can check it today.
- **Quotes:** in *"The food here is the best in Bandung," says Pak Hasan*, the words are **Pak Hasan's opinion**, not a fact. An article can report opinions.
- **Indonesian:** *menurut saya* = *in my opinion / I think*; *sebaiknya* = *should*; *paling enak* = *the best / the tastiest*.

id.text:
**Jebakan:**
- **Angka tidak otomatis membuat fakta.** *Rp50,000 is too much for a bowl of bakso* ada angkanya, tapi **too much** (terlalu mahal) adalah penilaian: opini.
- **Tebakan tentang masa depan adalah opini.** *Prices will probably go down next year* (harga mungkin turun tahun depan): tidak ada yang bisa mengeceknya hari ini.
- **Kutipan:** di *"The food here is the best in Bandung," says Pak Hasan*, kata-kata itu **opini Pak Hasan**, bukan fakta. Artikel bisa melaporkan opini orang.
- **Bahasa Indonesia:** *menurut saya* = *in my opinion / I think*; *sebaiknya* = *should*; *paling enak* = *the best / the tastiest*.

blocks.prompt: Read about a new library: which sentence is an opinion?
options: The library has more than 5,000 books.
The library should open on Sundays too.
blocks.explain: should shows what the writer thinks is a good idea: that's an opinion. You can check the opening time and count the books, so those are facts.

id.prompt: Tentang perpustakaan baru: kalimat mana yang merupakan opini?
id.explain: should (sebaiknya) menunjukkan apa yang menurut penulis bagus: itu opini. Jam buka bisa dicek dan jumlah bukunya bisa dihitung, jadi keduanya fakta.

blocks.text:
**Skimming** means reading fast to get the **gist**: the general idea of a text. You skim a news app in the morning, a long email from HR, or an article before you decide to read it carefully.
How to skim (about **1 minute** for a 100–120-word article):
- Read the **title** (and the photo caption, if there is one).
- Read the **first sentence of each paragraph**.
- Read the **last sentence**: it often sums up.
- Let your eyes run over **names, numbers and bold words**, but don't stop.
Then ask yourself: *What is this text about, in a few words?*

id.text:
**Skimming** artinya membaca cepat untuk menangkap **gist**: inti atau gambaran umum sebuah teks. Kamu melakukan skimming saat membuka aplikasi berita di pagi hari, membaca email panjang dari HR, atau melihat artikel sebelum memutuskan untuk membacanya dengan teliti.
Cara skimming (sekitar **1 menit** untuk artikel 100–120 kata):
- Baca **judulnya** (dan keterangan foto, kalau ada).
- Baca **kalimat pertama setiap paragraf**.
- Baca **kalimat terakhir**: sering berisi rangkuman.
- Biarkan matamu melewati **nama, angka dan kata yang dicetak tebal**, tapi jangan berhenti.
Lalu tanya dirimu: *Teks ini tentang apa, dalam beberapa kata?*

rows.note: after skimming, only the parts you need

id.note: setelah skimming, hanya bagian yang kamu perlukan

blocks.text: **The habit to break:** many Indonesian learners read word by word, translate every sentence in their head, or stop at every new word to open a dictionary. When you skim, don't! A new word in the middle of a paragraph rarely changes the gist. Try it with a timer on your phone: 1 minute, then say the gist in one sentence.

id.text: **Kebiasaan yang perlu diubah:** banyak pelajar Indonesia membaca kata per kata, menerjemahkan setiap kalimat di kepala, atau berhenti di setiap kata baru untuk membuka kamus. Saat skimming, jangan! Kata baru di tengah paragraf jarang mengubah intinya. Coba pakai timer di HP-mu: 1 menit, lalu sebutkan intinya dalam satu kalimat.

blocks.prompt: You have one minute for a 120-word article. What do you do?
options: Read every word and translate it.
Read the title and the first sentence of each paragraph.
Look up every new word in a dictionary.
blocks.explain: To get the gist fast, read the title and the first sentences: they usually carry the main ideas. Translating every word or using a dictionary takes too long for one minute.

id.prompt: Kamu punya waktu satu menit untuk artikel 120 kata. Apa yang kamu lakukan?
id.explain: Untuk menangkap inti dengan cepat, baca judul dan kalimat-kalimat pertama: biasanya di situ ide pokoknya. Menerjemahkan setiap kata atau membuka kamus terlalu lama untuk satu menit.

blocks.text:
Skim this article first (1 minute): the title, the first sentence of each paragraph, the last sentence. Then read it carefully and answer the two questions. (*sidewalk* = trotoar: American English; British English says *pavement*.)

**WALKING IN JAKARTA**
Walking in Jakarta is becoming easier. On Jalan Sudirman and Jalan Thamrin, the sidewalks are now wide and clean, with trees and benches. Rina, an office worker, walks 15 minutes from Dukuh Atas station to her office every day. "Two years ago I always took an ojek. Now I walk, and I save about Rp200,000 a month," she says.
Not every area is the same: in many parts of the city, sidewalks are still narrow or full of motorbikes. But I think the city is moving in the right direction, and other areas should follow.

id.text:
Skim dulu artikel ini (1 menit): judul, kalimat pertama setiap paragraf, kalimat terakhir. Lalu baca dengan teliti dan jawab dua pertanyaannya. (*sidewalk* = trotoar: bahasa Inggris Amerika; bahasa Inggris British memakai *pavement*.)

**WALKING IN JAKARTA**
Walking in Jakarta is becoming easier. On Jalan Sudirman and Jalan Thamrin, the sidewalks are now wide and clean, with trees and benches. Rina, an office worker, walks 15 minutes from Dukuh Atas station to her office every day. "Two years ago I always took an ojek. Now I walk, and I save about Rp200,000 a month," she says.
Not every area is the same: in many parts of the city, sidewalks are still narrow or full of motorbikes. But I think the city is moving in the right direction, and other areas should follow.

blocks.prompt: What is the main idea of 'Walking in Jakarta'?
options: Walking in Jakarta is becoming easier.
Sidewalks in Jakarta are full of motorbikes.
blocks.explain: The first sentence gives the main idea, and the rest supports it: wide sidewalks, Rina's walk. Rina's Rp200,000 is a detail. The text says sidewalks are full of motorbikes only in many parts of the city, not everywhere.

id.prompt: Apa ide pokok artikel 'Walking in Jakarta'?
id.explain: Kalimat pertama memberi ide pokoknya, dan kalimat lain mendukungnya: trotoar yang lebar, Rina yang berjalan kaki. Rp200.000 milik Rina adalah detail. Teksnya bilang trotoar penuh motor hanya di banyak bagian kota, bukan di mana-mana.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is the writer's opinion?
options: Rina walks 15 minutes to her office.
The sidewalks on Jalan Thamrin have trees and benches.
blocks.explain: should (and I think just before it) shows the writer's opinion. You can check Rina's walk and the trees and benches, so they're facts.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang merupakan opini penulis?
id.explain: should (dan I think tepat sebelumnya) menunjukkan opini penulis. Perjalanan Rina serta pohon dan bangku di trotoar bisa dicek, jadi itu fakta.

suggestedQuestions: How do I find the main idea if it isn't in the first sentence?
Is a sentence with a number always a fact?
What's the difference between skimming and scanning?
Should I look up new words when I skim?

resources.title: Digital habits across generations
resources.note: A B1 news-style article about how grandparents, parents and teenagers use their phones, with quotes from each. Good for finding the main idea of each paragraph. True/false and grouping tasks. Some sentences use grammar from later lessons: you don't need it for the gist.

id.note: Artikel bergaya berita level B1 tentang cara kakek-nenek, orang tua dan remaja memakai HP, dengan kutipan dari masing-masing. Cocok untuk mencari ide pokok setiap paragraf. Ada latihan benar/salah dan pengelompokan. Beberapa kalimat memakai tata bahasa dari pelajaran berikutnya: kamu tidak memerlukannya untuk menangkap intinya.

resources.title: The Martian: a book review
resources.note: A B1 book review: it mixes facts about the novel (the story, the film) with the reviewer's opinions. Try to mark each sentence F or O. Matching and multiple-choice tasks. Some grammar from later lessons.

id.note: Ulasan buku level B1 yang mencampur fakta tentang novelnya (ceritanya, filmnya) dengan opini penulis ulasan. Coba tandai setiap kalimat F (fakta) atau O (opini). Ada latihan mencocokkan dan pilihan ganda. Ada sedikit tata bahasa dari pelajaran berikutnya.

resources.title: How to spot fake news
resources.note: A B1 article with four tips for checking a news story online: look at the website, the photos and other news sources. A real-life use of 'Can I check this?'. Multiple-choice tasks. It uses some grammar from later lessons (for example the passive).

id.note: Artikel level B1 dengan empat tips untuk mengecek berita online: lihat situsnya, fotonya, dan sumber berita lain. Contoh nyata pertanyaan 'Bisakah aku mengecek ini?'. Ada latihan pilihan ganda. Artikel ini memakai beberapa tata bahasa dari pelajaran berikutnya (misalnya kalimat pasif).

id.intro: Hai! Di A2 kamu sudah membaca email, pesan dan berita pendek, dan mencari satu jawaban di dalamnya (scanning). Sekarang kamu membaca artikel pendek dan tulisan opini tentang hidup di Jakarta, pekerjaan, makanan dan transportasi. Kamu akan belajar tiga keterampilan: menemukan ide pokok, membedakan fakta dari opini penulis, dan membaca cepat (skimming) untuk menangkap inti teks.
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara menemukan ide pokok kalau tidak ada di kalimat pertama?
Apakah kalimat yang ada angkanya pasti fakta?
Perlukah aku mencari arti kata baru saat skimming?

assessment.ra-1: Baca artikel ini: 'FROM GARAGE TO BRAND · Five years ago, Bu Ratna made batik bags in her garage in Pekalongan. Today she has a small shop and twelve workers, and she sells shirts and scarves too. About 70% of her sales are online, mostly through Instagram and online marketplaces. Last year she started sending orders to Malaysia and Singapore. "I started with one sewing machine," she says. Her story shows that a small home business can grow into a real brand with the help of the internet.' Apa ide pokok artikel ini? Tulis dalam beberapa kata, dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.ra-2: Baca artikel ini: 'THE KRL IS GETTING BUSIER · Every year, more and more people are taking the KRL to work. Ani takes the 6:15 train from Depok to Manggarai every weekday. "Two years ago I always had a seat. Now I stand for the whole trip," she says. At her station, the number of morning passengers has gone up from about 8,000 to 11,000 a day. Many passengers want more trains in the morning, but some say the stations need more space first.' Kalimat pertama memberi ide pokoknya. Cari detail pendukungnya: berapa penumpang pagi di stasiun Ani sekarang?
assessment.ra-3: Baca kalimat dari sebuah blog makanan ini: 'At Rp45,000, a smoothie bowl is far too expensive for a normal breakfast.' Ini fakta atau opini? Tulis fact atau opinion.
assessment.ra-4: Baca komentar tentang MRT Jakarta ini: '(1) The MRT opened in March 2019, from Lebak Bulus to Bundaran HI. (2) At first it had 13 stations. (3) In my view, it is the most comfortable way to travel in Jakarta. (4) In 2019 a ticket cost between Rp3,000 and Rp14,000.' Kalimat mana yang merupakan opini penulis? Tulis nomornya.
assessment.ra-5: Lakukan skimming pada artikel ini dalam 30 detik: baca judulnya dan kalimat pertama setiap paragraf. 'THE CAFÉ IS THE NEW OFFICE · Every morning, Kopi Teman in Kemang is full of people with laptops. Freelancers, students and remote workers come at 9 and stay until the afternoon. / For many remote workers, a café is cheaper than a co-working space. A coffee costs about Rp30,000, and the Wi-Fi is free. / But some café owners are not happy about it. "One customer buys one coffee and stays for eight hours," says Bayu, the owner. Now he has a new rule: one drink every two hours.' Artikel ini terutama tentang apa? Tulis dalam beberapa kata, dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.ra-6: Lakukan skimming pada tulisan opini ini dalam 30 detik: 'WHY I MISS THE OFFICE · For two years I worked from home, and at first I loved it: no traffic, no uniform, lunch in my own kitchen. But slowly, things changed. I talked to my colleagues only on video calls, and I often worked late at night. Last month my company asked us to choose: home or office. I chose the office, four days a week. The trip is long, but I feel like part of a team again. In my opinion, home is for living, not for working.' Sekarang penulis lebih suka bekerja di mana? Tulis home atau office.
